common_name: Karma Choc Dahlia (Chocolate-Burgundy Waterlily Cut-Flower Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed following the last frost; stake at planting since stems can be lax under heavy bloom load.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed following the last frost. This Karma-series cut-flower dahlia produces waterlily-form double blooms 4–6 inches across in a velvety chocolate-brown shading to deep burgundy at the petal edges, an effect that intensifies in cool fall weather. Foliage and stems are notably dark, nearly black, echoing the flower tone. Bred specifically for the commercial cut-flower trade, Karma Choc holds up exceptionally well in the vase and blooms prolifically from midsummer through frost; stake plants since stems can be lax under heavy bloom load.

common_name: Mystic Illusion Dahlia (Black-Foliage Golden-Yellow Single Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed following the last frost; this compact series needs minimal staking.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed following the last frost. Part of the Mystic series bred for dramatic foliage contrast, this cultivar pairs deeply cut, near-black bronze-purple leaves with bright single, canary-yellow flowers that hold their color without fading. The open-centered blooms are attractive to bees and butterflies and make excellent cut flowers on strong, wiry stems held above the foliage. It blooms continuously from midsummer to hard frost and stays more compact than most border dahlias, so staking needs are minimal.

common_name: Otto's Thrill Dahlia (Giant Soft-Pink Dinnerplate Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed; sturdy staking is essential from planting time since flower heads are heavy.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed, staking sturdily from planting time since flower heads are heavy. A classic dinnerplate-type dahlia bearing enormous, fully double blooms 8–10 inches across, occasionally larger, in soft pink shading darker toward the center, with broad, symmetrically arranged petals that give the flower a lush, rounded form. It has earned numerous American Dahlia Society awards and a Royal Horticultural Society Award of Garden Merit for consistent bloom quality. Plants benefit from disbudding side buds to maximize bloom size.

common_name: Emory Paul Dahlia (Giant Orchid-Lavender Dinnerplate Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed; set a sturdy stake or cage at planting time to support the heavy flower heads.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed, setting a sturdy stake or cage at planting time to support the heavy flower heads. One of the largest-flowered dinnerplate dahlias grown, Emory Paul produces full, formal double blooms in orchid-lavender to fuchsia-pink that can reach 10–14 inches across under good culture. Like other giant dinnerplate types it blooms from midsummer to first frost and performs best with consistent moisture and monthly feeding. Dig and store tubers after frost in all but the mildest climates.

common_name: Bishop of York Dahlia (Golden-Orange Peony-Flowered Bronze-Leaf Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed; its more compact stature than many dahlias means lighter staking than dinnerplate types.

directions: Plant tubers horizontally 4–6 inches deep after soil has warmed. A member of the Bishop series that made 'Bishop of Llandaff' famous, this cultivar shares the same deeply divided, near-black bronze-purple foliage but carries semi-double, peony-form flowers in warm golden-yellow with a smoky orange center, exposing pollinator-friendly stamens. Blooms measure roughly 4–5 inches across on burgundy stems held well above the foliage from midsummer into early fall. Its more compact stature than many dahlias makes it useful for mixed borders and large containers without heavy staking.
